title: Remark, My Soul, the Narrow Bounds
description: Remark, My Soul, the Narrow Bounds in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 887 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Reflections for a New Year”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Re-mark, my soul, the nar-row bounds Of the re-volv-ing year; How swift the weeks com-plete their rounds! How short the months ap-pear!

lines: Remark, my soul, the narrow bounds
How swift the weeks complete their rounds!
Yet like an idle tale we pass
And study artful ways t' increase
Waken, O God, my trifling heart,
That I may act the Christian part,
And give the year to thee.
Thus shall their course more grateful roll,
Or this shall bear my peaceful soul

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
